english: For every subset $X$ of the set $\{1,2,3,\dots,12\}$, including the empty set and the whole set, the observation $d_{X}=n(X)-n(X')$ is recorded, where $X'$ denotes the complement of $X$ in $\{1,2,3,\dots,12\}$. Then the standard deviation of these $2^{12}$ observations is
hindi: समुच्चय $\{1,2,3,\dots,12\}$ के प्रत्येक उपसमुच्चय $X$ (रिक्त समुच्चय तथा पूर्ण समुच्चय सहित) के लिए प्रेक्षण $d_{X}=n(X)-n(X')$ लिखा जाता है, जहाँ $X'$ समुच्चय $\{1,2,3,\dots,12\}$ में $X$ का पूरक है। तब इन $2^{12}$ प्रेक्षणों का मानक विचलन है
solution: $d_{X}=2n(X)-12$. The value $n(X)=k$ occurs for $\binom{12}{k}$ subsets, so the frequencies of $n(X)$ are $\binom{12}{k}$, $k=0,\dots,12$
Dividing by $2^{12}$, these relative frequencies are the probabilities of $B\left(12,\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$: mean $6$, variance $12\cdot\dfrac{1}{2}\cdot\dfrac{1}{2}=3$
So the data $n(X)$ have mean $6$ and variance $3$; $d=2n(X)-12$ has variance $2^{2}\cdot3=12$ (shifting does not change variance)
solution_full: Frequency distribution of $n(X)$: exactly $\binom{12}{k}$ subsets have $k$ elements, $k=0,1,\dots,12$, and the total frequency is $2^{12}$.

The relative frequency of $k$ is $\dfrac{\binom{12}{k}}{2^{12}}=\binom{12}{k}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{k}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{12-k}$, which is the binomial distribution $B\left(12,\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$. The mean and variance of the data equal the mean and variance of this distribution: $\bar{x}=np=6$, $\sigma^{2}=npq=3$.
Effect of a linear change on ungrouped data: if $y_{i}=ax_{i}+b$ then $\sigma_{y}^{2}=a^{2}\sigma_{x}^{2}$. With $a=2$, $b=-12$: $\sigma_{d}^{2}=4\cdot3=12$, and the mean of $d$ is $2\cdot6-12=0$.
Hence $\sigma_{d}=\sqrt{12}=2\sqrt{3}$. (Option (C) is the variance and option (A) is the standard deviation of $n(X)$, both typical slips.)
originality_note: New: a data set indexed by all subsets of a 12-element set, whose frequency table is the binomial coefficients, so the standard deviation of the data is read off from the variance of B(12, 1/2) and then rescaled (way 5: binomial mean and variance linked with the variance of ungrouped data). Closest known: 'variance of the first n natural numbers' and 'mean and variance of B(n, p)'. Different because: the student must recognise the binomial distribution inside a data set that does not mention probability.

concept_use.Mean and variance of a binomial distribu: The relative frequencies C(12,k)/2^12 form B(12, 1/2), whose mean 6 and variance 3 are used.
concept_use.Standard deviation and variance of ungro: The standard deviation of the 2^12 observations is found with the rule that y = ax + b scales the variance of ungrouped data by a^2.
